findings.text: The dry-run path calls dispatch_picker_selection unconditionally, so a shadow-mode preview still asks the picker and spends its latency — the done-when clause 'a dry run in shadow mode does not call the picker at all' is unmet. The file is owned by the concurrent node gc-reports-what-it-already-did, so it is outside this node's write scope and the node correctly reported it under follow_ons; the landed change keeps the report comparable regardless, so this does not hold the node.

The reviewed manifest names its gate logs under test_logs but carries no baseline_suite/after_suite fields, so the read-time annotation (reckon/crew/review.py:1314, annotate_review_of_run) finds neither log and read_review reports added_failure_count as unmeasured even though both gate logs are complete. The count in this review's stored record was therefore derived by hand from logs/gate-base.log and logs/gate-head.log.

The comparability guard masks every key ending in _at wholesale rather than only the picker's observation stamps, so a per-call picker field whose name ended in _at would be excluded from the comparison instead of caught; the intended latency_ms/jev_latency_ms fields do not end in _at and are covered, so this is a widening of the mask rather than a gap in what it was added to catch.
